texts.facts: The accident took place with a vehicle bearing registration No. DL- 1ZC-4033 driven and owned by respondent no.1, Sh. Kailash Kumar and insured with respondent no. 2, Go Digit General Insurance Company Limited. BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE: 2. The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR and the claim petition are that the information of an accident was received at P.S. Burari vide DD No.63A. ASI Roop Singh along with Ct. Praveen went to Sushruta Trauma Centre Hospital where they found that the injured Chet Singh was admitted in the said hospital and they collected his MLC no. 23357/21. On asking the injured to give his statement, he refused to do the same as he was in severe pain due to the accident in question. After some days, the injured gave his statement to the IO that he was working as Supervisor in Capital Company, Bhagirath Palace, Chandni Chowk, Delhi and that on 17.07.2021 at about 10:15 AM, he was standing outside the godown at main 100 Foota Near Ullas Vatika, Shalimar Palace, Delhi when suddenly respondent no. 1, driver of the offending vehicle i.e. Taxi bearing no. DL-1ZC- MACT No. 499/2022 Chet Singh Vs. Kailash Kumar and anr. Page 2 of 37 4033, came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the injured due to which he sustained grievous injuries. Thereafter, CATS Ambulance reached at the spot and took him along with his friend Pankaj to the Sushruta Trauma Centre Hospital, where the injured got his medical treatment. Notice under Section 133 M.V. Act was issued to the registered owner. Thereafter, driver of the offending vehicle was apprehended and on enquiry, arrested. Since the offence was bailable, he was released on bail on furnishing of bail bonds. The offending vehicle was seized by the IO and sent to Malkhana. The DL and RC of the offending vehicle were taken into the custody of the IO. The mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle could not be done. The documents pertaining to the offending vehicle were found to be correct after verification from the concerned authority. Therefore, on the basis of MLC of the injured, case was registered under section 279/337 IPC and investigation was initiated. IO had collected the MLC of the injured after final opinion and the injury was shown as 'grievous' on the MLC of the petitioner and therefore, section 338 of IPC was added. On completion of investigation, chargesheet under section 279/338 IPC was filed against the driver Kailash Kumar and DAR was filed before the court on 23.05.2022. 3. Despite various opportunities, respondent no. 1 failed to file his written statement and therefore, his right to file the same was closed vide order dated 24.04.2023. Respondent no. 2 insurance company filed the reply on 08.12.2022. and anr. Page 3 of 37 EVIDENCE 4. To prove its case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1. The petitioner closed his evidence. Respondent no. 2 examined Sh. Paramvir, Legal Officer as R2W1. RE was closed vide order dated 12.03.2024. 5. The Petitioner filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner has been recoded. Final arguments were heard on behalf of the petitioner and respondent no. 2. FINDINGS & OBSERVATIONS 6. In this matter to prove the occurrence of the accident as well as the rashness and negligence on the part of the driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1, the petitioner (PW-1) in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A had deposed as under:- "1... 2. That due to sheer negligence of respondent no. 1 this accident was occurred and the injured/dependent suffered grievous injury as per the MLC, caused by respondent no. 1 which cannot be compensated in terms of money. 3. That the deponent was/is working with Capital Company, Bhagirath Palace, Chandni Chowk, Delhi as Supervisor. On unfortunate day, on 17.07.2021 at about 10:15 am the deponent was standing outside MACT No. 499/2022 Chet Singh Vs. Kailash Kumar and anr. Page 5 of 37 of the Godown of Havells India Pvt. Ltd. Main 100 Foota near Ullas Vatika, Shalimar Palace, Burari, Delhi in the meantime one offending vehicle Taxi bearing no. DL-1ZC-4033, which was driven by the respondent no. 1 came in a very high speed, zig zag rash, negligent, carelessness manner and hit the left foot of the deponent forcefully and at very high speed, the deponent and motorcycle fell down. Due to very heavy impact, the deponent fell down on the road and the deponent received grievous injuries due to the said heavy impact. The respondent no. 1 ran away from the spot. Mr. Pankaj who was with the deponent at the site. Pankaj came at the spot and called at 112 number, thereafter CATs Ambulance B- 65 took the deponent at Sushruta Trauma Centre Hospital, Delhi at that time Mr. Pankaj was with the deponent. The deponent was given treatment at Sushruta Trauma Centre Hospital, Delhi. The attending doctors of Sushruta Trauma Centre Hospital, Delhi prepared MLC no. 23357/2021 of the deponent, which clearly indicates the grievous injuries left proximal tibia fracture, abrasion on all over body of the deponent. The deponent is still under treatment from different Hospitals. 4. That the deponent is suffering with intolerable pain and agony, during the entire periods of treatment from the above said hospitals. The deponent/injured has spent all his savings as well as lent some money from his friend and relatives for medical treatment but the respondents have not paid compensate to the deponent/injured till date. 5. That the deponent is earning livelihood for his family members and at the time of his accident, he Chet Singh (I) ( Fir 621/21 Burari) vs Kailash Kumar (Go Digit) on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168030185/ 4 sustained grievous injuries left proximal tibia fracture, abrasion on all over body and during the period of treatment in the hospital, his family members have to face tremendous harassment and mental paid and agony and the treatment of the deponent is still continues and subsists. 6. That the respondent no. 1 is the driver and owner of offending vehicle Taxi bearing no. DL-1ZC-4033, who was driving the offending vehicle in a very most rash, negligent, reckless and zig zag manner at a very high speed without any regard from the traffic rules or any concern for human safety. The respondent no. 2 is the insurer of the offending MACT No. 499/2022 Chet Singh Vs. Kailash Kumar and anr. Page 6 of 37 vehicle Taxi bearing no. DL-1ZC-4033. Both the respondents jointly and severally liable to compensate the deponent/injured for his better treatment. The accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver/respondent no. 1. 7. That the police officials investigated the matter at site of accident thoroughly and after thorough investigation, the police official registered a FIR no. 621/2021 dated 29.07.2021, u/s. 279/337 IPC PS Burari Delhi against the respondents, which is on record. 8. That at the time of accident, the deponent was 47 years old, possession good health and sound mind and robust physique and was not suffering from any kind of ailment or addicted to any voice. Occupationally, the deponent/injured at the time of accident, the deponent was working with Capital Company, Bhagirath Palace, Chandni Chowk, Delhi as Supervisor and earning for a sum of Rs. 21,000/- per month from the said work. But due to heavy impact, the entire activities of the deponent have come to standstill and now the deponent is completely confined to bed. Due to the several multiple injuries, the deponent is not able to attend his daily routine work and is lying on bed taking continuous treatment. 9. That the deponent has spent Rs. 65,000/- on his medical treatment and Rs. 50,000/- on conveyance and Rs. 50,000/- on special diet. The deponent has suffered permanent disability. The life of the deponent has bee shortened due to the accident. The deponent will have to spend Rs. 1,00,000/- for future treatment. The deponent/injured is also entitled to get compensation of Rs. 20,000/- . ... Chet Singh (I) ( Fir 621/21 Burari) vs Kailash Kumar (Go Digit) on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168030185/ 5 12. That the claim of the deponent is well within the ambit of MV Act 1988 and the deponent is very well entitled for the reliefs as claimed by him against the respondents and the contents therein stated, are true and correct. That it is my true and correct statement. 13. That I say that the deponent is entitled to get compensation Rs. 20,00,000/- as he sustained grievous injuries." 10. PW-1, has proved the factum of the accident and the identity of the respondent no.1. He has unequivocally testified that respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-1ZC-4033 in a rash and negligent manner which led to the accident in question. He has deposed that on 17.07.2021 at about 10:15 AM, he was standing outside the Godown of Havells India Pvt. Ltd. Main 100 Foota near Ullas Vatika, Shalimar Palace, Burari, Delhi when the offending vehicle Taxi bearing no. DL-1ZC-4033, driven by respondent no. 1 came in a very high speed, zig zag rash, negligent, carelessness manner and hit the left foot of the injured. He has also deposed that he has received grievous injuries due to the said accident. No convincing material has been brought on record by the respondents to show that no accident took place or that respondent no. 1 was not rash and negligent while driving the offending vehicle. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 1,00,000/- under this head. The offending vehicle was being driven and owned by respondent no. 1 Kailash Kumar and insured with respondent no. 2, Go Digit General Insurance Co. Ltd. 42. Respondent no. 2 examined Sh. Paramvir, (Legal) of the insurance company who proved the notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC as well as the postal receipts issued to Respondent no. 1 to produce a valid permit but despite due service, he did not produce the same.
texts.arguments: Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287). In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as MACT No. 499/2022 Chet Singh Vs. Kailash Kumar and anr. Page 4 of 37 required in criminal cases. In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. In this regard, reliance is placed on the judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the cases of Teja Singh Vs Suman & Ors., MAC. APP. 1111/2018 & CM APPL. 52384/2018, 52386/2018, date of decision 06/12/2019; MAC. APP. 428/2018, titled as The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Kamla Devi & Ors, date of decision 08.11.2019 and MAC. APP. 690/2017 & CM APPL. 28108/2017, titled as Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Mona & Ors., date of decision 15.10.2019, which had relied upon the judgment in the case of Cholamandalam Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs Kamlesh 2009(3) AD Delhi 310. 12. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the charge-sheet for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC and other relevant documents against the respondent no. 1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no. 1 Kailash Kumar (driver cum owner of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probability. Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment Chet Singh (I) ( Fir 621/21 Burari) vs Kailash Kumar (Go Digit) on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168030185/ 7 for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), Chet Singh (I) ( Fir 621/21 Burari) vs Kailash Kumar (Go Digit) on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168030185/ 8 (ii)(a) and (iv). We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation (see for example, the decisions of this court in Arvind Kumar Mishra vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. - 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M., National Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2010 (8) SCALE 567). 9. An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 50,000/- under the head conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. The petitioner Chet Singh has claimed loss of future earning to the extent of Rs. 3,60,360/- in his Form XIV. It has already been established that the petitioner has suffered 26% disability in relation to his left lower limb. Since, the left leg of the petitioner has sustained permanent disability to the extent of 26% disability and the capacity of the petitioner to stand properly has been gravely affected, the functional disability of the petitioner shall be assessed at 13% in relation to the whole body. The income of the petitioner has been assessed as Rs. 15,908/- as on the date of accident. Thus, he was more than 47 years old and less than 48 years of age. Accordingly, the Multiplier of thirteen (13) is taken for purposes of calculating the loss of income of the petitioner (Reliance is placed on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Pranay Sethi & Ors., Special Leave Petition (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, date of decision - 31.10.2017). Further, by adopting the principles laid down in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC), the future prospects of Manish Kumar shall be 25% as he was self employed and was in between the age bracket of 40 and 50 years at the time of accident on 17.07.2021. 32. In the case of Benson George v Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. in Civil Appeal No. 1540 of 2022 decided on 25.02.2022, Hon'ble Supreme Court had awarded an interest of 6% per annum.
